correctness.rationale: A finite-index exponent lattice has an exact heat kernel obtained by summing a finite residue numerator over two geometric denominators. This gives the stated Laurent coefficients, including c2=1/(h log r log s). Splitting the lattice zeta by residue classes reduces vertical-strip control to the unrestricted lattice zeta and finitely many shifted double sums, which are handled by Euler-Maclaurin and Hurwitz-zeta bounds. The prime-weight remainder is no larger shell-by-shell than in the unrestricted lattice. The established Mellin, Ingham and saddle calculation therefore carries through with the recomputed lattice data. The dependent r^q, s^q, rs family is exactly the congruence lattice A congruent to B modulo q. Symbolic and finite exact checks corroborate the residue formulas and collision identity.

originality.rationale: Golafshan's September 2026 theorem treats the unrestricted two-generator exponent lattice and explicitly requires multiplicative independence to avoid repeated indices. The present theorem treats arbitrary fixed full-rank finite-index exponent sublattices and derives the universal h^{-1/3} leading factor. Neyt's 2017 slides use a broad generating-set formulation, but their displayed product transform counts representations rather than distinct generated elements when multiplicative relations are present, so it does not establish the collision-constrained set result. Equivalent-formulation searches did not locate prior coverage. Residual risk remains from unindexed concurrent work and unpublished material related to the older slide announcement.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a single unrestricted exponent lattice to every fixed finite-index sublattice while retaining a full relative-error-o(1) strong asymptotic and explicit multiplicative constant. It separates the universal covolume effect, h^{-1/3} in the leading logarithmic coefficient, from finer boundary arithmetic in lower terms. The dependent generators r^q, s^q and rs give a concrete collision application and show why formal generator rank can predict the wrong growth dimension.
